dossier.public_summary: This 13.3-day dip around a bright spotted K dwarf is not on target proof, but it alternates deep then shallow between transits, lacks a consistent depth, and disappears in later sectors, exactly as expected for spot-driven or blended binary systematics on a star rotating every 6.2 days. The secondary eclipse and odd/even difference support a binary or systematics explanation over a 1.6 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even depths differ strongly (619.6 ppm odd vs 313.7 ppm even, difference 305.9 ppm, ratio 2.0), with sector_oe_max_sigma 11.49 and 3 sectors over 3 sigma same sign share 0.6667. Indicates binary at twice period, not a planet.
Secondary dip at phase 0.2383 depth 85.33 ppm with snr 4.002, secondary_over_bump 0.9601; marginal detection consistent with stellar companion, not a planetary occultation.

Individual transit depths highly inconsistent (chi2 265.565, dof 6, share_of_top_3 0.989). Epoch 1 1103 ppm (9.1 sigma) and epoch -136 1219 ppm (8.1 sigma) much deeper than mean 465 ppm, with later sectors near zero (-19 ppm, 41 ppm). Signal not repeatable.

Sector depths change dramatically (471, 411, 629, -19 ppm, depth_change_pct 173.7) and sector_depths_by_source verdict differs_by_source shows QLP sector 104 depth -19 ppm vs SPOC 2-min mean 483 ppm. Even within SPOC 2-min p_constant 0.03712380397105051 not steady.

Star is highly variable (amplitude 5741-7455 ppm, false_alarm 0.0) with rotation_d ~6.1815, signal period 13.3 d ~2.16x rotation. Phase_curve amplitude 27.71 ppm ratio_to_depth 0.05798 chi2 16.63 indicates activity. Combined with flat-bottom shape v_sigma -3.448 but high impact parameter fit_b 0.9581 and duration ratio 0.5291, variability drives apparent but non-repeatable transits at harmonic periods.
